content:
Apple will release its fiscal year 2026 third quarter results on Monday, November 2. Here are the expected highlights.

Price hikes are expected to play a major role

Apple today confirmed that it will release its fourth quarter (2026) results on Monday, November 29.

Following the release of quarterly results, the company will hold a conference call at 2:00 p.m. Pacific Time / 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time. New CEO John Ternus is expected to participate for the first time, alongside Apple CFO Kevan Parekh.

In the fourth quarter of the previous fiscal year, Apple reported revenue of $102.47 billion, up 8% year-over-year, and earnings of $27.47 billion — a substantial 87% increase from the $14.7 billion recorded in Q4 2024, primarily benefiting from a $10.2 billion one-time tax provision related to Apple's long-running tax dispute with Ireland.

In its previous quarter's results, Apple indicated it expected fiscal year 2026 Q4 revenue to grow 9% to 11% year-over-year, despite facing a 2.5 percentage point negative impact from foreign exchange, as well as significantly intensified supply constraints on iPhone, Mac, and iPad.

If this holds true, Apple's revenue would fall between $111.69 billion and $113.74 billion. Apple also expects gross margins between 47% and 48%, down from 50.1% in the previous quarter — though that previous quarter's figure included roughly two percentage points of benefit from tariff refunds.

In practice, Apple's quarterly results will, for the first time, fully reflect the comprehensive impact of the steep price hikes on its hardware lineup implemented at the end of June.

It is worth noting that, as this fiscal quarter closed at the end of September, the results figures are unlikely to meaningfully reflect market demand for the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max — both similarly raised-priced new devices that only went on sale on September 18.

That said, Apple's results will reveal how the company has navigated memory constraints and rising component costs for another quarter, laying the groundwork for Ternus's first full quarter as CEO (results to be released at the end of January).
